native-jax-fp8-state-overwrite-maintaine.review_kind: fresh independent maintained-source and correctness review

maintained_pieces.reason: The default apply_overwrite hook preserves the previous whole-object overwrite behavior for other CustomGradientAccumulation subclasses, including Int8DotGeneralOp. Dispatch belongs at the existing state application boundary used by take_train_step. This is a small reusable extension of the existing protocol rather than a research-only workaround.

Selecting the latest active metadata copy prevents an inactive later microbatch from discarding active scales. Maximum reduction still preserves new amax values and the common rolled history tail. Zero is the identity for the nonnegative histories.

The per-leading-layer all-six-array zero test handles real AD zero cotangents without identifying a legitimate zero amax or one zero field as inactivity. The final vector-axis reduction preserves arbitrary stacked leading axes produced by the existing quantization constructor. The same rule is used for accumulation and persisted-state application.

A public behavior regression uses real differentiation, scan accumulation, partitioning, persisted-state application, and a subsequent FP8 forward. Unused and alternating activity reproduce the actual corruption; active-zero guards legitimate zero updates and rolled histories. Assertions check all six state arrays, ordinary-weight preservation, exact subsequent output, and explicit placement. No mocks, historical benchmark harness, or research-only constants are promoted. The TPU marker requests hardware placement coverage while retaining supported CPU execution.

static_analysis.all_six_identity: Fp8DotGeneralOp has exactly six dynamic array fields; compute_dtype/fwd_dtype/rev_dtype are static. Each supported constructor leaf has a final metadata-vector axis and shared stacked leading dimensions.
static_analysis.active_zero: in_q_bwd and quantized_dot_bwd carry updated scales and rolled histories independently of numeric zero cotangents. With valid positive-scale state, active zero work is not the all-six-zero identity and the roll is retained.
static_analysis.numerical_masking: The new predicate matches exact zeros only. NaNs and infinities are not classified inactive. There is no tolerance, clipping, nan_to_num, operand change, or dtype conversion in the new logic.
static_analysis.placement: The new computation reduces only each metadata vector's final axis and broadcasts the layer mask to the original leaves. Existing constructor/vmap shape conventions are coherent with this. CPU4 regression artifacts support explicit-mesh behavior; this review makes no accelerator claim.
static_analysis.scope: Only quantization.py and test_fp8.py differ from the named base. No configuration, launcher, numerical kernel, or research artifact is included.

Existing evidence establishes CPU regression behavior and explicit CPU mesh placement, not TPU/GPU numerical or runtime behavior.

The mask relies on the existing final-vector-axis and shared-leading-shape invariant of Fp8DotGeneralOp state. No supported caller violating it was found, so this is an invariant rather than an actionable defect.

No separate direct-unused single-microbatch regression is added, but the same apply_updates hook is exercised by the all-unused scan case and the new code's direct path was inspected. This is not a demonstrated defect.

behavior_assessment: For nonquantized models, the Haliax partition selects no dynamic ordinary leaves into state, so the supplied JMP cast sees the same ordinary arrays and reconstitution preserves NamedArray boundaries and static structure.

For CustomGradientAccumulation subclasses, the complete state object is removed before casting and reinserted without a dtype conversion or value rounding; the fix is not specific to one FP8 field or one model.
Weights and other ordinary floating arrays still reach the original JMP policy cast. Nonfloating arrays and ordinary static leaves retain JMP behavior.

Trainability filtering can leave partially populated custom-state objects on either side; each helper retains those objects atomically, and the final existing TrainerState combine merges their ordinary leaves as before.

Jitted callback and model-loader lambda replacements preserve original mapping and compute-policy selection. No quantization algorithm, scale update, custom VJP or optimizer update implementation changes.

All cast_to_compute occurrences in lib/levanter/src/levanter now pass models through the helper, including the model-loader callback. Remaining direct cast_to_param sites are model initialization/loading or export before quantization installation, not an omitted maintained compute boundary.

The changed test oracle casts only the known projection weight and does not reuse the production helper or partition routine. Exact loss and all differentiable leaves compare against that independent precision control. The metadata is intentionally not BF16-representable.
Checkpoint continuation compares the entire resulting state against uninterrupted execution; this is observable numerical/persistence behavior, not a helper-dispatch or implementation-mirroring test.
